title: Build a STANDALONE repro for: does `Diff.diff` retain the trees it walks? This decides whether the wata-mac idle leak (MAC-IDLE-LEAK) is our bug or a sgola one, so it must stand on its own with no app around it. WHAT IS KNOWN: wata-mac's windowed live heap after each GC climbs 1 2 4 6 8 11 14 18 21 24 27 31 34 MB over 39 collections (~200 MB/hour, ~5 days to the observed 26 GB). A pump bisect narrowed it to the diff call: with patchTo/setTree skipped the series is FLAT (0 0 0 1 0) even though a fresh tree is still built every frame; with `Diff.diff` running and NOTHING encoded and NOTHING handed to the backend, it leaks. The heap profile in that state shows the retained objects are the VIEW nodes (sgolaNewColon2__Keyed 47%, WataLogic_contactRowView cum 65%) while Diff itself is ~515kB of pathOf path lists. So it is not the patches. WHAT TO BUILD: a spike beside tools/objc-spike and tools/interp-spike (own dir, own sgo.build, a `just` recipe), whose whole body is a loop calling Diff.diff and measuring. Judge it with runtime.ReadMemStats HeapAlloc read AFTER an explicit runtime.GC() every N iterations, not with RSS — RSS is a sawtooth the scavenger drives and it is what made this leak read as 'steady' for a whole session. Print the series; a leak is a straight line, a bounded working set plateaus. THE FOUR ARMS, and the comparison is the point: (a) build two trees per iteration and DO NOT diff them — the control, must be flat, and if it is not the finding is about tree construction and this ticket is misaimed; (b) build a fresh tree per iteration and diff it against a tree allocated ONCE outside the loop — this is the app's shape, where `old` is long-lived (st.last) and `new` is fresh; (c) diff two trees BOTH allocated once outside the loop, so nothing fresh is walked — if this leaks the retention is not about the argument's age; (d) as (b) but discard the result immediately (`val _ =`), to see whether holding the returned List[Patch] for even one iteration matters. SHAPE THE TREES LIKE THE APP'S: a VGroup of a few KEYED children over VText/VRect leaves, with one field differing so the patch list is non-empty — an empty diff may take a path that never touches the nodes. Keys matter because the child scan is the keyed path. WHAT THE ANSWER MEANS: if (b) or (c) leaks, the retaining edge is below wataui/diff.scala — that module has no global state, every binding in it is a local var — and this becomes a sgola inbox ticket carrying the repro and the series, since a compiler that retains what a pure function walked is a defect no consumer can work around. If all arms are flat, the leak needs the app, and the next suspects are what the app adds: st.last held ACROSS the call, and whether the emitted code lets patches escape.

CONFIRMED LEAK, bisected to the DIFF STEP; the retaining edge is the one thing left. Verified in the WINDOWED app (the shape the owner's 26 GB happened in) over ~11 min: live heap AFTER each GC goes 1 2 4 6 8 11 14 18 21 24 27 31 34 MB — a straight line over 39 collections, no plateau. ~3.4 MB/min = ~200 MB/hour = 26 GB in ~5 days, which matches 'days of running'. THE BISECT (headless, which leaks the same way): everything -> leaks; tree built but patchTo/setTree skipped -> FLAT (0 0 0 1 0), which is the control and also rules out WataLogic and the client snapshot; Diff+Wire computed but nothing sent to Go -> leaks, ruling out macshell.Apply and the retained AppKit backend; Diff.diff ONLY, no encode, nothing sent -> still leaks. The heap profile in that last state shows the retained objects are the VIEW NODES (sgolaNewColon2__Keyed 47%, WataLogic_contactRowView cum 65%) while Diff itself accounts for ~515kB of path lists — so diffing a tree is what makes THAT TREE stay reachable, and every frame's tree is then held. The pump retains exactly one (st.last) and contactRowsView builds only visibleRows() rows, so neither explains it. NEXT: a standalone repro — loop Diff.diff over two fixed trees with no app around it. wataui/diff.scala has no global state (every binding is a local var), so if the standalone loop leaks this is BELOW the Sgola source and becomes a sgola compiler ticket rather than our bug. `just mac-leak` now has --windowed, --heap, --goroutines, --vmmap, and judges on the live-heap series rather than RSS

title: the `-page_duration 20000` flag in tools/make-chirp.py is now INERT and should go at the next regeneration. It existed because the old reader took a page's payload as one frame, so an ffmpeg-default chirp read as a single oversized frame; Ogg.readFrames walks the lacing table now and the asset would be correct without it. It cannot simply be deleted: the asset is committed as BYTES and `--check` has to keep reproducing them, so the flag comes out only when the chirp is next re-encoded from the owner's source recording (which lives on the owner's machine only). Nothing breaks meanwhile — this is a tidy-up whose trigger is someone else's file

FILED upstream 2026-08-08 — the sgola inbox has it; this line tracks OUR side until a ruling comes back. The trigger fired: with leg (1) pinned (40cc1f8) objc-spike builds and the binary RUNS to `panic: stub` in Main_cstr, so the address question can be tried rather than guessed. The signature `def cstr(s: String): go.Uintptr` already compiles — go.Uintptr as a result type was settled by b85a713 — it is the BODY that is open, and it is open for a real reason: go.Uintptr was ruled opaque because a uintptr is not a reference and does not keep its referent alive, which is exactly what makes taking a String's address hard. Go's own answer is unsafe.Pointer + syscall.BytePtrFromString, where the *byte's pointer-ness is what holds the bytes. We asked for an address whose referent is live for the enclosing facade call, and said we would accept a restriction to argument position only (both our uses are arguments). Does NOT block us today — no shipping wata code calls C through purego — but it gates the macOS/iOS FFI story

the HANDSET half of the arrival notification. The MODEL IS SETTLED and shared: `wataclient/src/main/scala/notify.scala` owns NotifyMode (NotifyPlayNow/NotifyQuiet), Arrival, and Notify.step — the arrival edge is a conversation's unplayed count rising, priming is once per SESSION (a DM room is created by its first message, so per-conversation priming silences the arrival most worth having), and the mac's decisions are pinned by `wata-fb notifytest` in ci plus `just mac-notify-smoke`. What is left is wata-fb's presentation of the same two modes: PLAY IMMEDIATELY walkie-talkie style — except when the volume knob is off, which is also the screen-off/silent position — and a quiet mode that blinks the LED, shows an in-app banner and HIGHLIGHTS the conversation rather than only bumping a count, which a kid is unlikely to notice. Reuse the mac's auto-play shape too: the same ActPlay plus WataLogic.withPlaying, so the existing AePlaybackDone arm sends the read receipt

title: the red recording bar should carry a mini spectrum-analyzer / level animation driven by the LIVE capture level, so holding PTT visibly proves the mic is working. Motivated by 2026-08-07: `DEC1 MUX` reset to ZERO and every message recorded four seconds of digital silence that sent, arrived and played as nothing — the recording overlay counted up happily throughout, because it animates on the CLOCK, not on audio. A meter fed from the encoder's input frames would have shown a flat bar the moment the kid spoke. Wants: the level computed where the PCM already is (the audio thread, before Opus), carried to the UI as a small int on the existing event/mailbox path rather than a new channel, and drawn with the view algebra's rects so it costs nothing on the 160x128 panel and works on the mac backend unchanged. Same bar on both clients
